Trail running shoes

Trail running shoes grip loose gravel, wet roots and packed dirt far better than road shoes, because their lugs are deeper and their rubber is softer.

Most of the pairs below have a rock plate under the forefoot, a gusseted tongue that keeps grit out, and a toe bumper for scrambling. Lighter models suit fast races on dry, groomed trails.

Heavier, more cushioned models suit long days in the mountains. If you are not sure which drop or stack height you need, our fitting guide explains how to choose, and every pair can be returned within sixty days.
